Against reflow2:fact:predictions-for-the-reading-budget-runs-registered-before-any-run-2026-10-29. Blind-scored (scores-budget.tsv, scores-cue.tsv), Sonnet answering agents, one run per arm.
(b) ONE READING BUDGET, score/25 (cites): 12 KB: notes 14.5 (0, it cited a batch range), reflow2 5.5 (0); reflow2 + one-line cue to its state records 17.5 (3). 36 KB: notes 22.5 (24), reflow2 15.5 (0). Unbudgeted pilot: notes 24.5, reflow2 25.
(c) TRACEABILITY (pilot answers, can a person follow support from the memory): reflow2 25, notes 25, summary 12.5. Steps: reflow2 23 of 25 found in one search and one to three nodes; notes 11 of 25 needed walking back through batch sections.
(d) TWO PASSES: structuring (six writing rounds) summary 386k tokens / 8 min, notes 478k / 10 min, reflow2 1,082k / 49 min; using (one unbudgeted answering round) 57k, 98k, 164k; budgeted answering ~54–73k for both arms.
PREDICTIONS: P6 (reflow2 +3 at 12 KB) REFUTED, notes led by 9; P7 (gap ≤2 at 36 KB) REFUTED, notes led by 7; P8 (both below unbudgeted) HELD; P9 (reflow2 +5 traceability) REFUTED, tied, though reflow2 was faster to trace; P10 (using within 30%) HELD under budget, not unbudgeted (1.7×).
READING: structure did not pay at a budget by itself; what decided it was whether the reader was told where the current state was kept (root cause: reflow2:fact:root-cause-a-budget-limited-reader-was-not-cued-to-the-designs-current-state-record-2026-10-29). With that one cue, reflow2 beat notes at 12 KB. The structure's visible advantage was speed of tracing, not whether tracing was possible.
